> [!reminder] How this scene works
> The Fell wake with no memory. Every Fell rolls three checks: Renewal to get up, Lore to know where they are, and Vigilance to see around them. Then Kettle, a Shrewish child, finds them, the floor shows the first sign of the root, and Nib calls them upstairs. Nothing here is decided yet. The scene ends when the Fell go up the stairs.

> [!readaloud] Opening: Under the grain
> Weight on your chest, and dust in your mouth. You are lying under sacks, a lot of them, and they smell of barley. Somewhere close, a lot of small voices are talking at once. Under your back the floor is humming. It is a low, steady sound that you feel in your teeth. Something light is standing on your chest. It weighs about as much as a cat.

> [!reminder] How a skill check works
> Explain skill checks to your players. A Fell rolls 1d6 + the skill's competency. You roll 1d6 + 0. Higher wins, and a tie is your call. A 6 is a Fellmark: it succeeds, and their skill increases by 1. A 1 is a Fellstrike: it goes wrong. Every Fell rolls each check below for themselves.

> [!lorecheck] Renewal: Getting up
> Every Fell rolls. They have been asleep somewhere they did not lie down, and their bodies want to stay there.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You sit up and the sacks slide off you. Your head is clear. A dozen small faces stare up at you, whiskers twitching, and one of them is already holding out a cup of water with both paws. *Then:* Their Renewal increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* You shove the sacks off and sit up. Stiff, dusty, and in one piece.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You get up on the second try. The room tips, then settles. Your legs don't want to hold you.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You heave yourself up and a sack splits open over your head. Barley pours down your collar and into your ears. Somebody small laughs and then stops quickly.

> [!lorecheck] Lore: Where am I
> Every Fell reaches for anything that fits.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* Small whiskered people. Roots overhead. A cellar packed with food. Shervinaw, the world of the giant trees, and these are the Shrewish. You know that the roots here open and close their tunnels on their own, and that the Shrewish never go anywhere without a week of food. And something else comes up with it, something of your own. *Then:* Hand this Fell their Lore Drop on a card, as [[Secrets and Lore Drops]] sets it out. Their Lore increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The little people are Shrewish. This is Shervinaw. You don't know how you know it.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* Nothing. Small people, a cellar, sacks. None of it means anything to you.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You know exactly where you are. You fell asleep in a granary at home, and in a minute someone you know will come down those stairs and laugh at you. You're sure of it. *Then:* This memory is false, and only you know it. Note it on your memory card for this Fell, as [[The Fell Who Forgot]] sets out: nobody they know is coming. The first person down the stairs is Nib.

> [!lorecheck] Vigilance: Looking around
> Every Fell rolls, once they are sitting up.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* A low cellar with a stone ceiling, stone walls, and roots growing through the gaps in the stone. Sacks, barrels, strings of dried mushrooms. A dozen Shrewish, none of them taller than your knee, all of them carrying something. Stairs going up. And across the floor, a crack you can put your finger in. The air coming out of it is warm and smells of wet, rotten wood. *Then:* Their Vigilance increases by 1. This Fell knows the crack is warm, which no one else here has noticed.
> - **Success.** *Read:* A stone cellar full of food and full of Shrewish, a dozen of them, none taller than your knee. Stairs going up. A crack across the floor.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* Dust and lamplight, sacks and small people. You can't make out much more than that.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You are certain there is a second way out of here, a little door behind the barrels. There isn't. You spend a while looking.

> [!readaloud] Kettle
> The thing on your chest is a child. A Shrewish child, the size of a rat, in a knitted jumper with the sleeves rolled four times. She has a lamp twice as big as her head and she is holding it right up to your face.

> [!dialogue] Kettle
> "You're awake! Grandad said you were dead, and Mister Hobb said you were drunk, and I said you were asleep, and I was right, so I get to keep you. I'm Kettle. Are you very strong? You look very strong. Can you lift that barrel? Don't lift it yet, I want to watch."

> [!dialogue] Kettle
> *If asked where they are:* "You're in Brackenmouth, silly, in the barley cellar. Everybody's in Brackenmouth tonight. The whole of the Slumpwood came down the river, my grandad says, because it's stone here and the rot can't get stone. It's very crowded. Somebody's goat is in the bread room."

> [!dialogue] Kettle
> *If asked how they got here:* "I don't know. You were just here, under the barley. Nobody knows where you came from. Mister Hobb thinks you came down the river. I think you came out of the ground."

> [!lorecheck] Lore: The Slumpwood and the rot
> Any Fell who asks what the rot is, or what the Slumpwood is.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* The blight. A grey rot in the living roots of Shervinaw. A rotted root goes soft and grey, closes its tunnels on whoever is inside, and grows over anything warm. The Slumpwood was a forest east of here, and this spring it went grey all at once. *Then:* Their Lore increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The blight. A rot in the roots here that makes them go grey and soft. The Slumpwood is a forest it took.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You don't know. Kettle tells you anyway: "It's the grey. It makes the roots go soft and shut, and then they eat you. Not really eat. Grow on you. It's bad."
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You are sure the rot is a sickness people catch, and you take a step back from the Shrewish. Kettle looks hurt. *Then:* It isn't. The rot is in the roots, and only the roots.

> [!beat] The floor
> The hum under the floor rises. Everyone in the cellar goes still. The crack in the floor opens a finger's width, and through it, for a moment, everyone sees grey bark move. It is wet and soft, and it gives where it touches the stone. Then it closes. The Shrewish all start talking at once.

**This applies to a Shrewish Fell.** The Shrewish in the cellar take them for a cousin from another warren, and they talk to them first and fastest. One of them hands this Fell a sack to carry before saying hello.

**This applies to a Fell with a Felionis.** The Shrewish go quiet around the cat and give it room. Kettle does not. She tells it it is a good cat.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *From the top of the stairs, loud:* "Is that the big ones? Are they up? Good. You, the tall ones, all of you, up here now. I need anything that can lift a stone, and I need it five minutes ago."

> [!readaloud] Closing: Up the stairs
> You climb out of the cellar with barley in your hair and a child the size of a rat hanging off your sleeve. Behind you the crack in the floor has closed again, and the humming goes on under the stone. Up the stairs, a lot of small voices go quiet, waiting for you.

> [!choice] What the Fell do
> - **Go up the stairs.** Go to [[02 - Nib|Nib]].
> - **Look at the crack first.** They find warm, soft grey wood under the stone, and it moves away from their fingers. Then Nib shouts again. Go to Nib.
> - **Stay in the cellar.** Kettle tugs at them until they go, and if that fails Nib comes down to get them. Go to Nib.
> - **Leave by some other way.** There is no other way. The stairs are the only way out of the cellar. Go to Nib.
